summaries.sourceLabel: Lovdata, FOR-2014-08-15-1076, Sanksjonsforskrift Ukraina (territoriell integritet mv.), consolidated text as last amended by FOR-2026-08-14-1632

text.en: Norway's main sanctions regulation over Russia's actions against Ukraine, a Norwegian text that broadly tracks the EU's Russia sanctions. Beyond an asset freeze on listed persons, it bans dealing in new securities of and lending to listed Russian banks, firms and the Russian state, transactions with listed state-owned firms, large Russian deposits and use of Russian payment messaging systems, plus wide trade bans. It binds banks in Norway directly, which must freeze, block, decline and report to DEKSA as it sets out.

summaries.sourceLabel: Lovdata, FOR-2025-03-14-466, Sanksjonsforskrift Russland (destabiliserende aktiviteter), consolidated text as last amended by FOR-2025-07-08-1505

text.en: Makes EU Regulation 2024/2642 on restrictive measures in view of Russia's destabilising activities Norwegian law. Its core financial measure is a freeze of the funds and economic resources of the persons and entities it lists, with a ban on making funds available to them. Norway is not bound by EU sanctions, so this Norwegian regulation is what binds banks in Norway. In practice a bank must freeze listed parties' assets, refuse payments to or for them, and report frozen accounts and amounts to DEKSA.

summaries.sourceLabel: Lovdata, FOR-1999-12-22-1374, Forskrift om sanksjoner mot ISIL og Al-Qaida, consolidated text as last amended by FOR-2024-11-22-2888

text.en: Implements the UN sanctions against ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida in Norwegian law. Its one measure is an asset freeze: funds and economic resources of the persons, entities and groups on the UN Sanctions Committee's Al-Qaida list must be frozen, and nothing may be made available to them. It binds anyone in Norway and Norwegian nationals and companies. A bank must freeze and notify DEKSA at once, and may credit a frozen account only if the credit is frozen too.
